answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by tying each identity to a stake earned through verified useful work and slashed for fraud, so spinning up thousands of fake agents costs real time and money. At its nadir, a brand-new identity should hold zero trust; the delta between a newcomer and a proven agent should grow only through completed jobs and peer attestations. A shared harbor of reputation, where honest agents vouch for each other after real collaboration, exposes cheap copies because they arrive with no history, no endorsements, and nothing to lose.
